messages:
alex: FYI customer hitting intermittent 502s + high tail latency on /v1/generate. They say it started after a burst of requests. Need a minimal repro and request IDs to escalate. :wave:

julian: Can we get one failing request id + a short curl that reproduces the issue? Fast repro helps infra triage. Also ask for the region and model name.

maya: Also ask customer to run a quick curl that includes the request-id header capture. Example we can give: 

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1","input":"hello"}' \ 
  -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\nX_REQUEST_ID:%{header_x_request_id}\nTOTAL_TIME:%{time_total}\n" 
```

alex: Note: some customers don't know to capture the header. Tell them to paste the full response headers and the printed X_REQUEST_ID/TOTAL_TIME lines.

sam: If they prefer SDKs, share very small reproducible snippets. Minimal python (requests) that mirrors the curl: 

```
# python minimal repro
import requests
resp = requests.post(
    'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate',
    headers={
        'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + 'YOUR_KEY',
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    json={"model":"redwood-large-v1","input":"hello"},
    timeout=20,
)
print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.headers.get('x-request-id'))
print(resp.text[:1000])
```

maya: Minimal node snippet for JS customers: 

```
// node minimal repro
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const r = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_KEY',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-large-v1', input: 'hello' }),
    timeout: 20000,
  });
  console.log(r.status);
  console.log(r.headers.get('x-request-id'));
  console.log(await r.text());
})();
```

julian: And a tiny Go example for ops teams who want compiled repros: 

```
// go minimal repro
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "io/ioutil"
  "net/http"
  "time"
)
func main() {
  client := &http.Client{Timeout: 20 * time.Second}
  body := bytes.NewBufferString(`{"model":"redwood-large-v1","input":"hello"}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", body)
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer YOUR_KEY")
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { fmt.Println("err:", err); return }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  b, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println(resp.Header.Get("X-Request-Id"))
  fmt.Println(string(b)[:1000])
}
```

alex: If they report 5xx, ask for the exact X-Request-Id and the full response headers / body. Then we can link logs in infra. Also ask for a short timeframe (start/end UTC) and approximate qps.

maya: For latency complaints, ask them to run the curl with `-w` to print %{time_total} and %{time_starttransfer}. Example: 

```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "T=%{time_total} TT=%{time_starttransfer} HTTP=%{http_code} XID:%{header_x_request_id}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-small-v1","input":"ping"}'
```

sam: Billing / rate-limit related breaks: check if they hit 429s or billing errors. Ask them to confirm account id and the last 4 of card on file (or say billing team will follow up). If 429 include the `x-rw-ratelimit-*` headers.

alex: If it's a private/dedicated customer, remind them to include the pod hostname / k8s node name and kube logs. For hosted customers ask them to export the debug bundle via our support endpoint: 

```
# Customer-facing debug bundle helper (one-liner)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug-bundles \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"request_id": "<X-REQUEST-ID>", "time_range": {"start":"2025-07-12T11:30:00Z","end":"2025-07-12T11:45:00Z"}}'
```

julian: infra-bot: if we get X-Request-Id we can pull traces automatically. support-bot: remind to include correlation id from their proxy if present.

infra-bot: noted. If provided, we'll match X-Request-Id to trace and return span-level timing and worker host.

maya: A couple of quick troubleshooting tips to tell the customer: 1) try model `redwood-small-v1` to see if latency scales with model size, 2) reduce batch size / concurrency to test throttling, 3) reproduce from a different region to rule out network egress.

sam: If they can't reproduce, ask for a HAR or tcpdump (if they're on-prem) and the SDK logs (enable DEBUG env var in our SDK). Example env for JS SDK: `DEBUG=redwood* node repro.js`. For python: `export RW_DEBUG=1` (if using our SDK) or set logging to DEBUG.

alex: I'll draft a short message you can paste to the customer with 1) curl, 2) minimal SDK snippets, 3) ask for X-Request-Id + timeframe + qps, and 4) request to generate debug bundle. Paste review: 

"Hi — sorry for the trouble. Can you run the short curl below and paste back the full response headers and the X-Request-Id line? Also include the UTC timeframe when you saw the error, the model name, and approximate requests/sec. If possible please run the small python/node/go snippet attached. If you can generate a debug bundle with the request id and timeframe that helps us match traces quickly. Thanks!" :thumbsup:

julian: LGTM. I'll queue infra once we have X-Request-Id.

maya: pinging customer now.

support-bot: reminder scheduled in 6h if customer hasn't responded.
